cases.situation: My friend Tara sent me her wedding speech draft for her sister, asked for honest thoughts. It's sweet but 7 minutes long and half of it is inside jokes nobody will get.
cases.reply: I read it twice and the bit about teaching her to ride a bike on Elm Street made me tear up, keep that exactly as it is. Where I got a bit lost was the middle, with the camp stories: I didn't know the references, and I think a lot of the room won't either. If you kept one of those and cut the rest, you'd land around four minutes and the bike story would hit even harder. This is going to be lovely.
cases.note: Specific praise first, one main issue as her experience as a listener, one concrete fix, and the goal restated.

cases.situation: 我带的实习生小吴做了一份竞品分析PPT，下周要给总监汇报。数据很扎实，但结论埋在第15页，前面全是表格。她没主动问我意见。
cases.reply: 小吴，汇报前想给你一点意见，你想听吗？数据这块做得很扎实，特别是价格对比那张表，比我们之前的都清楚。我唯一的担心是结论在第15页，总监很可能前面就开始问'所以呢'。要不要把第15页的三条结论挪到第2页，后面的表格作为支撑？这份东西底子很好，调一下顺序就会很出彩。
cases.note: 对方没主动问，先征得同意；只挑最重要的一条，给一个具体改法。

cases.situation: Gave my brother feedback on his food truck business plan, said the location costs look way too low. He got defensive and said 'I thought you'd be supportive'.
cases.reply: I can hear that landed harder than I meant. It's one person's take, and I only said it because I think the truck could really work and I'd hate for rent to be the thing that trips it up. Happy to drop it, or go through the numbers together over a beer on Saturday, your call.
cases.note: Don't retract the point and don't add to it. Reaffirm the goal and offer to leave it there.

cases.situation: A peer on my team, Ben, ran our sprint retro for the first time and asked me afterwards for honest feedback. It was well organised, but he kept moving on before the quieter people, Jun and Aroha, finished their points.
cases.reply: Thanks for asking. The way you pulled the action items together at the end was really clear, it's the first retro where I knew exactly who owned what. One thing I noticed: when Jun and Aroha started to speak, the discussion moved on before they'd finished, and I don't think their points made it onto the board. Maybe a quick round where everyone gets a minute before the open discussion? I'm only raising it because these retros are getting genuinely useful.
cases.note: Describe what you saw, not a trait ('you talk over people'), and give one fix he can try next sprint.

cases.situation: Ma responsable Claire a demandé à chacun un retour honnête sur la nouvelle réunion d'équipe du lundi. Elle dure 1h30 et la première moitié, c'est la lecture de chiffres qu'on reçoit déjà par mail le vendredi.
cases.reply: Merci de demander, Claire. Ce qui marche vraiment, c'est le tour de table sur les blocages : grâce à lui, j'ai réglé le souci de facturation avec Karim en dix minutes. Là où je décroche, c'est la première partie, parce que les chiffres sont déjà dans le mail du vendredi. Et si on partait du principe que tout le monde l'a lu, en gardant seulement les questions sur ces chiffres ? On finirait sans doute en 45 minutes, avec le meilleur de la réunion.
cases.note: Retour vers sa responsable : un point fort précis, un seul problème vécu, une proposition formulée en question.

cases.situation: Hired a freelance designer, Amara, for our cafe logo. The first round of 3 concepts came in and none feel right, they're all very corporate. Round two is included and I don't want to crush her.
cases.reply: Hi Amara, thanks for these. The lettering on concept 2 is lovely, and I can see the care in the spacing. Seeing all three together made me realise they feel more corporate than we are: we're a tiny neighbourhood cafe with mismatched mugs and a chalkboard menu, so I think the logo should feel hand-made and warm. Could round two push in that direction, maybe starting from the concept 2 lettering? Happy to do a 15-minute call if that's easier.
cases.note: With a paid creative, describe the direction you want, not just 'not quite it', and keep one real thing to build on.

cases.situation: 我爸退休后开始写回忆录，写完前三章发给我，说想听听真实意见。有些段落写得很好，但大部分是按年份一件件记流水账，读着有点累。
cases.reply: 爸，前三章我认真看完了。写您1978年进厂当学徒那段特别好，师傅让您拿锉刀锉了一整天铁块，我读的时候好像都能听见那个声音。我读着有点吃力的是后面几章，一年一年往下记，事情一多，反而看不出哪些对您最重要。要不每章就挑一两件您印象最深的事，像锉铁块那样展开写？这本东西值得写好，以后我想拿给朵朵看。
cases.note: 对长辈也是一样：先说一处真实具体的好，再只提一个问题，用'我读着'描述感受，最后回到这件事的意义。

cases.situation: My friend Dani did her first open mic last week and asked what I thought. I told her the dentist opener killed but the middle bit about dating apps felt like stuff we've heard before. Now she's texting 'so you thought it was bad?? just tell me it was good'.
cases.reply: I don't think it was bad. The dentist bit was the best thing I heard all night, and people were still quoting it at the bar. The middle isn't there yet, and I think it can be, which is the only reason I said it. If you want a cheerleader for the next one, just say and I'll be the loudest person in the room.
cases.note: When they push you to say it was good, hold the point without adding to it, and offer to be the cheerleader next time if that's what they want.

cases.situation: My 17-year-old son Eli asked me to read his college essay, due Nov 1. It's all about winning the state debate final and reads like a résumé. The one paragraph about his grandpa driving him to practice at 6am is the only part that sounds like him.
cases.reply: I read it twice. The paragraph about Grandpa driving you to practice at 6am is the best thing in it; that's the part that sounds like you. Where I lost the thread was the rest, which tells me what you won more than who you are, and I'd guess admissions readers see a lot of trophy essays. What if the whole essay grew out of those car rides? It's your essay and your call. I'm only saying it because I think there's a really good one in here.
cases.note: With your own teenager: one point, framed as a reader's experience, and the decision handed back. It's his essay, not yours.

cases.situation: 闺蜜小雨准备在相亲软件上重新写个人资料，发给我让我提真实意见。照片选得挺好，但自我介绍全是“不要抽烟的”“不要妈宝男”这种，读下来像在设门槛。
cases.reply: 你问我真实意见，那我就直说啦。照片选得特别好，第二张在大理骑车那张，一看就是你。最可以改的是自我介绍：现在写的大多是“不要什么”，读下来有点像在设门槛。要不改成三件你真正喜欢做的事，比如周末爬山、做饭请朋友吃？我是觉得你这么有意思的人，资料应该让人一眼就看出来。
cases.note: 先说一个具体的优点，只挑最重要的一个问题，用“我读下来的感受”来讲，再给一个能直接改的建议。

cases.situation: My friend Nadia just launched her jewelry shop on Etsy and posted the link in our group chat. The pieces are lovely, but the photos are dark and shot on a busy floral tablecloth. She didn't ask for feedback.
cases.reply: Nadia, congrats on the launch! The hammered silver hoops are gorgeous, I'd wear them tomorrow. I've got one small thought about the photos if you want it, or I can just be your cheerleader today. Either is fine.
cases.note: Unasked means ask first, and in a private message, not the group; if she says yes, give only the one point: daylight and a plain background.
